title: Existing-entry updates preserve the old modality and bypass the rule gate
evidence: The gate checks incoming modality at 88; the update branch at 94-97 changes content, version and attestation but never entry.modality.
trigger: Insert an attested DeonticRule, then insert the same key with EpistemicFact and has_biometric_attestation=false.
impact: The stored entry remains DeonticRule with replacement content and no attestation. Conversely promoting an existing fact with an attested rule leaves it typed as a fact. This is a local buffer invariant failure; downstream effect authorization was not established.

title: State commitment omits boundaries between key and content
evidence: state_digest feeds k.as_bytes() immediately followed by entry.content.as_bytes(), without lengths or separators (144-145).
trigger: Compare singleton buffers with key="a", content="bc" and key="ab", content="c", and identical modality/version/frequency/attestation.
impact: Different buffer states feed identical bytes to BLAKE3 and therefore have equal commitments without breaking the hash. The digest cannot uniquely bind the represented state.

title: Zero-capacity governance buffer still accepts an entry
evidence: new accepts max_capacity=0 (56-60); insert evicts an empty map when len>=0 and then inserts unconditionally (101-114).
trigger: Construct SessionGovernanceBuffer::new(0) and insert an EpistemicFact.
impact: The buffer returns success and contains one entry despite its configured zero capacity. CapacityExceeded exists but is never returned.

title: FD exhaustion test also passes when target operation succeeds
evidence: Descriptor duplication stops after 5001 even if exhaustion was not reached; the only result assertion is inside if let Err(e) = res.
trigger: Run with a soft descriptor limit above the fixed duplication cap.
impact: Test can report success without entering EMFILE or validating failure under actual exhaustion, leaving the named failure path untested.

title: Cross-device rejection test compares a device ID with itself
evidence: test_nemesis_v12_mount_boundary_exdev_fail_closed asserts q.dev == q.dev and checks only the display string of a constructed CrossDeviceUnsupported error. It never supplies a different mount or invokes an operation expected to return EXDEV.
trigger: A regression removes cross-device rejection from the backend.
impact: This named security regression test still passes because none of its assertions exercise the rejection behavior.

title: Concurrent revocation test asserts a locally manufactured abort
evidence: The revocation thread stores true and is joined before the branch; the true branch constructs EffectTxState::Aborted and asserts it equals itself. It neither revokes an orchestrator authority nor dispatches a guarded operation.
trigger: A regression disables actual revocation enforcement.
impact: test_nemesis_v09_concurrent_capability_revocation remains green without testing revocation or any concurrent operation against the orchestrator. The simulation is labelled in a comment but cannot support the suite security-coverage claim.

title: Queue failure handler references an unbound exception
evidence: except sqlite3.Error at line 99 does not bind exc; exc is assigned only if the nested fallback fails at line 115.
trigger: An enqueue fails after db_path has already switched to _fallback_path.
impact: Logging raises UnboundLocalError instead of returning the documented graceful queue failure.

title: Half-open circuit admits every concurrent caller
evidence: can_execute changes OPEN to HALF_OPEN for the first caller, but returns True unconditionally for all subsequent HALF_OPEN callers.
trigger: Concurrent decorated calls arrive after recovery_timeout while the first probe is awaiting its network result.
impact: The recovering endpoint receives concurrent probes rather than the claimed single trial, defeating throttling during recovery.

title: Hash the artifact bytes before reporting the artifact verified
evidence: artifact_hash_ok compares artifact.sha256 text only with manifest.artifact_hash; no artifact bytes are opened.
trigger: An artifact is modified while the bundle hash strings remain unchanged, then this verifier is used to assess it.
impact: ARTIFACT HASH is reported VERIFIED without checking the artifact that the audit purports to bind.

title: Make the attestation verdict depend on verification results
evidence: VERDICT is printed as EMPIRICALLY_CONSTRAINED_PASS and HW PROVENANCE as SECURE_ENCLAVE_TRNG_NOMINAL unconditionally; all_ok is calculated afterward at line 137.
trigger: Any component or signature check fails, or a software-generated signing key is supplied.
impact: Human-readable output still declares PASS and hardware provenance, contradicting the checks; exit status does fail for failed checks.

title: Preflight suppresses compilation failure and still approves
evidence: cargo check failure is consumed by || echo; the script continues to its unconditional APPROVED message and exit 0 when the following script returns success.
trigger: cargo check exits nonzero while enforce_c5_rules.sh returns zero.
impact: Callers receive successful environment validation for a workspace that did not compile.

title: Environment preflight also changes remote branch protection
evidence: The environment validation calls ./scripts/enforce_c5_rules.sh, whose lines 17-37 execute gh api --method PUT on /repos/borjamoskv/BABYLON-60/branches/main/protection, with no opt-in argument.
trigger: A user runs preflight with an authenticated gh account able to administer the repository.
impact: A routine validation invocation can change remote review and branch-protection policy. This is a traced side effect, not evidence that it has occurred.

title: Filesystem event arithmetic overflows before burnout can be observed
evidence: event.paths.len() as u8 * 10 and inferred u8 entropy_injected += surprise_value (lines 45-49) use unchecked narrow arithmetic.
trigger: A single event carries at least 26 paths, or accumulated per-tick path counts exceed 25.
impact: Debug execution panics; release arithmetic wraps and can suppress or lower the injected value, invalidating the demonstrated overload behavior. This is an example, not a finding about the production scheduler.

title: Simulated tier stress test certifies IDE behavior it never exercises
evidence: Mocks at lines 15-38 return constant strings after sleeps; loop 96-99 runs sequentially; line 117 unconditionally declares IDE never blocked and empirical falsification passed.
trigger: Run the PoC successfully, including cases where its mock latencies differ from real inference or IDE behavior.
impact: Output can be mistaken for verification of actual IDE availability although no IDE state or real inference path is checked.

title: Idle eviction uses tenant age instead of inactivity
evidence: idle_time = now - scope.created_at; TenantScope.created_at is set only when registering a new tenant. AgencyHypervisor.project_event does not update an activity timestamp.
trigger: Call evaluate_and_evict after max_idle_seconds while the tenant continues processing events.
impact: The active tenant is deleted by evict_tenant despite recent activity; subsequent project_event calls return False and its in-memory queue loses registration. This is an API-level defect; no deployed scheduler was established.

title: List samples generate object-only MCP schemas
evidence: isinstance(val, (dict, list)) sets p_type="object". to_json_schema emits that type directly; mcp_scaffolder.py:147 maps object to dict and :152 embeds the schema.
trigger: Deduce a contract from sample_calls containing an args value such as [1,2].
impact: Generated tool schema rejects the same array-shaped argument it was inferred from, breaking tools that accept lists.

title: Watchdog uses a predictable writable script path
evidence: open("/tmp/alert_v5.scpt", "w") follows symlinks and later os.system executes the same shared path (21-24).
trigger: Another local user precreates the path as a symlink before this PoC runs, or swaps its contents between write and osascript.
impact: Can overwrite a file writable by the runner or execute attacker-chosen AppleScript with runner privileges.

title: Remove the shared bearer credential from the launchd template
evidence: Plist embeds a literal bearer credential. tools/babylon60_mcp.py:975–996 reads this environment variable and :873 compares incoming authorization to it. Credential value intentionally omitted.
trigger: Deploy this launchd template unchanged.
impact: Anyone with repository/template access knows the bearer credential for that deployment; loopback limits network reach but does not make the shared value secret. No deployment or exploitation was tested.

title: Convert milliseconds and forward latency to the correct sensor argument
evidence: sample signature is (current_tokens, step_duration_s=1.0, ipc_latency_ms=0.5) at line 38; verify_action passes estimated_latency_ms as positional second argument.
trigger: verify_action evaluates an action using estimated_latency_ms.
impact: The burn rate uses milliseconds as seconds (underestimating it by 1000 for positive durations), while IPC latency remains 0.5 ms and cannot trigger the intended latency barrier.

title: Consolidation deletes journal rows without saving their replacement
evidence: JournalEntry.load returns only the ID (26-27), merge discards payloads (30-32), save is pass (34-35), then DELETE executes at 51. database.core.connect uses isolation_level=None.
trigger: Call autoconsolidate against a nonempty journal table.
impact: Every selected original entry is deleted with no replacement persisted; autocommit makes deletion durable even before the final commit.

title: Bootstrap reports operational success when daemon is absent
evidence: The missing-executable else branch only echoes a compilation instruction; line 60 unconditionally reports bootstrap completed and operational status.
trigger: Run this example without the prebuilt poc_sovereign_spark_daemon_bin while the .cortex directory exists.
impact: Shell success and operational message misrepresent a failed bootstrap; automation cannot distinguish missing daemon.

title: Commit polisher invokes nonexistent rewrite script path
evidence: _rewrite_commits invokes scripts/rewrite_commits.py; targeted filesystem read reports absent. Actual matching implementation is scripts/c5_git_utils/rewrite_commits.py.
trigger: Polisher reaches rewrite after reviewer and optimizer succeed.
impact: Rewrite subprocess fails and polisher loops failure recording; configured rewrite functionality does not run.

title: Adversarial campaign rejects labels instead of exercising independent gates
evidence: Gate 2 rejects on adversarial_type == INTENT_TAMPERING even without checking evidence. PRECONDITION_MISMATCH and ENTROPIC_SLUDGE modify payload after digest calculation (151-158), so Gate 2 rejects them before gates 3/4; gates 3/4 themselves branch on labels at 199/215.
trigger: Campaign outputs are used to claim the named precondition, Shannon filtering and authority isolation controls were verified.
impact: A 100% rejection report does not establish those controls; two scenarios do not reach their named gates, and the broker is harness-local. This finding concerns test validity, not a production bypass.

title: Swarm entry point imports a module absent after renaming
evidence: Imports legion_swarm_core; filename search finds scripts/c5_sharur/sharur_swarm_core.py only. That module defines run_legion_swarm at line 63.
trigger: Execute the CLI directly in the repository without an unrelated external module on PYTHONPATH.
impact: ModuleNotFoundError prevents CLI execution.

title: Claimed monotonicity accepts positive energy increments
evidence: The printed dH/dt <= 0 check uses np.diff(energy_ph) <= 0.05, while the final verdict is printed unconditionally.
trigger: A trajectory has energy increases up to 0.05, or any check evaluates false.
impact: The demonstration reports monotonicity or eradicated divergence without establishing either property; this is a toy numerical trajectory, not a model evaluation.

title: Native host integration reads can block indefinitely
evidence: read_frame(timeout_sec=2.0) ignores timeout_sec and calls blocking proc.stdout.read(4) and read(length) at lines 53 and 57.
trigger: Child remains alive but fails to produce a complete response frame.
impact: Test hangs before reaching the bounded proc.wait or finally cleanup.

title: GitHub Actions secret example embeds secret directly in shell program
evidence: The YAML run script interpolates secrets.API_KEY directly into echo "${{ secrets.API_KEY }}" before shell evaluation; unlike the token at 167, the secret value is not passed through an environment variable.
trigger: Use this example with a secret containing shell expansion syntax such as a literal command substitution.
impact: The runner interprets secret contents as shell code, causing unintended command execution or corruption of the value being stored.

title: Forensic protocol treats a wish to remember as mathematical proof of lying
evidence: Stage 3 takes statements such as Ojalá me acordase and requires proving latent information and a lie by analogy to an unmapped pointer; no formal memory model or proof is supplied.
trigger: Apply Stage 3 to a person who remembers an event occurred but cannot recall its detail, and wishes to remember.
impact: Protocol mandates a false deception conclusion: reference to an unknown detail does not establish possession of that detail. This affects documentary audit guidance, not a demonstrated runtime detector.

title: Fail the audit gate when Python source cannot be parsed
evidence: extract_python records SyntaxError and performs only regex import salvage (232-239); analyse stores syntax_errors separately (1162); main --fail-on examines rep["findings"] only (1253-1254), so syntax errors never affect exit status. render also prints an all-imports-resolve statement whenever findings is empty (1212-1213).
trigger: Audit a repository with a malformed Python source file containing no regex-recoverable imports, using --fail-on alto (or any severity).
impact: The command emits syntax diagnostics but exits zero and can print an all-imports-resolve message despite being unable to inspect the source; a CI consumer relying on the gate accepts incomplete audit coverage. This is a static control-flow result, not an executed reproduction.
